jobs.title: Promovendus PhD position Ecology of waterway management We have five positions available with the new BALANS project in The Netherlands: three PhD positions (at Radboud University (RU), at University of Groningen (UG) and at FLORON/RAVON), one 4-year postdoctoral position (RU) and one two-year position for a research assistant that will open later in 2027 (UG). These positions are part of a larger project funded by LVVN (Dutch Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Food Security and Nature) dedicated to the management of waterways. Waterways such as ditches are maintained to ensure sufficient water flow capacity, but also harbour important biodiversity. BALANS will generate knowledge on best practices for future management of waterways, searching for a balance between waterway’s practical functionality and their biodiversity. The results will be used for the revision of the new code of conduct for waterway management in the Netherlands (2029) and are obtained in in a consortium that includes RU, RUG, FLORON, RAVON, and Wageningen Environmental Research (WEnR), with project management by STOWA (Foundation for Applied Water Research), and guided by a committee that includes representatives from the Dutch waterboards and species conservation NGOs. jobs.title: Promovendus PhD position Placing the Local Group in a cosmological context Understanding how our Milky Way and its nearest neighbors formed is a central theme of modern Astrophysics, and one for which our group at the University of Groningen has worldwide recognition. The field of Galactic Archaeology uses the detailed fossil record of stars in our Galaxy, M31 and their satellites to reconstruct this history. It is currently undergoing a revolution thanks to the Gaia satellite and to massive spectroscopic surveys. However, we are currently missing sufficiently realistic cosmological simulations to fully interpret and exploit these datasets. Thanks to a recent development by our international team, producing such very realistic analogues of the Milky Way and M31 is within reach. Such high-resolution cosmological simulations of the evolution of gas, stars and dark matter with state-of-the-art codes, will allow us to quantitatively link the observed spatial, dynamical, and chemical structure of the Milky Way and M31 to their assembly history and environment and provide new tests of the standard cosmological model. jobs.title: Promovendus PhD position RSO TraFFIC - AI and Space Domain Astronomy The University of Groningen (UG) partners in the national project Resident Space Object Tracking For Fusion, Inference, and Characterisation (RSO TraFFIC). It aims to improve the tracking and characterisation of objects in Earth orbit. The Groningen contribution is led by Dr Gijs Verdoes Kleijn of the Kapteyn Astronomical Institute and Dr Eduardo Balbinot (Center for Information Technology and Kapteyn Astronomical Institute). The 2.6 Meur 6 year project brings together the universities of Delft, Groningen, Leiden and Radboud, the Royal Netherlands Aerospace Centre (NLR) and the space companies Dunedain and Ecosmic. Modern society depends on space-based infrastructure, but Earth’s orbit is becoming increasingly crowded: about 40,000 objects are catalogued, two-thirds of all spacecraft ever launched have gone up in the past seven years, and more than a million untrackable fragments between one and ten centimetres—each large enough to destroy a satellite—are in orbit. This makes it more difficult to monitor what is happening in space and to prevent collisions. The RSO TraFFIC project will address these challenges by combining data from different sensors and developing new sensing techniques and algorithms to track objects and examine the legal and governance frameworks needed to manage Earth orbit as a shared resource in a safe, sustainable and responsible way. jobs.title: Promovendus PhD position in Atmospheric Sciences (Trace Gas Observations) Trace gases are important constituents of Earth’s atmosphere impacting on climate, the ozone layer and human health. In this project you will perform analysis of trace gas mixing ratio observations from the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere. You will mainly rely on data from the long-term passenger aircraft project IAGOS-CARIBIC, which deployed scientific instrumentation during regular passenger flights over more than a decade. The dataset has been used to derive climatologies of trace gases in the upper troposphere and lowermost stratosphere, and it was found to be largely representative for that purpose. In this project, you are going to focus on special events that are characterized by unusual trace gas mixing ratios, in particular long-lived greenhouse gases but also other tracers. The aim is to identify and characterize such events, understand their origin and the meteorological processes causing them, as well as their likelihood and impacts. jobs.title: Postdoctoraal onderzoeker Postdoctoral Researcher – Living Evidence Synthesis, Systematic Reviews and AI-supported Evidence Research Are you an experienced researcher with a passion for evidence synthesis, systematic review methodology and innovative approaches to scientific knowledge integration? Do you want to contribute to an ambitious international research programme aiming to improve the understanding and clinical use of biomarkers and endpoints related to reward, motivation and impulsivity across major depressive disorder, Alzheimer’s disease and obesity? The University of Groningen is looking for an enthusiastic and scientifically strong Postdoctoral Researcher in Living Evidence Synthesis, Systematic Reviews and AI-supported Evidence Research. In this position, you will play a central role in developing and maintaining a structured living evidence framework that continuously integrates new scientific knowledge with emerging findings from a large, interdisciplinary research programme. You will combine advanced systematic review and meta-analysis methods with innovative approaches to evidence surveillance and large language model (LLM)-supported research. This is an exciting opportunity for a researcher who wants to work at the intersection of evidence synthesis, clinical research, biomarker science and artificial intelligence, while contributing to research with potential relevance for patients, clinicians, regulators, health technology assessment bodies and healthcare systems. jobs.title: Postdoctoraal onderzoeker Postdoc Additive manufacturing of Lightweight Alloys A one-year postdoc position is open in the Advanced Production Engineering (APE) research group at the Engineering and Technology Institute Groningen (ENTEG), Faculty of Science and Engineering. The appointment will focus on additive manufacturing of lightweight alloys. Additive manufacturing (AM) offers virtually unlimited possibilities to realize any desired geometry. It is especially suitable for producing complex structures and internal features that cannot be manufactured using conventional subtractive processes. A current limitation of AM is the degraded dimensional control and surface integrity of specific surfaces. The objective of this SNN project is to enable high quality and high precision additive manufacturing of aluminum alloy components by addressing product structure, AM process and material properties related challenges in an integrated solution. The outcomes include material-centric design guidelines for geometric optimization to compensate shape deviation, post-AM heat treatment for tailored microstructure and experimentally validated physical model relating microstructure and material properties to the performance of stainless steel prints. jobs.title: Promovendus PhD position in Systems and Control Theory for Energy-based Learning Are you excited about developing new mathematical foundations for energy-efficient computing? Do you want to contribute to cutting-edge research at the intersection of systems and control theory, optimization, circuit theory, and neuromorphic computing? The University of Groningen is seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to work on a fundamental research project on systems and control theory for learning in neuromorphic circuits. Neuromorphic computing is an analog, brain-inspired computing paradigm with the potential to drastically reduce energy consumption while enabling faster inference than conventional digital architectures. A major challenge, however, is the development and analysis of dedicated algorithms for training analog circuits directly from data. In this PhD project, you will develop a novel system-theoretic framework for learning in analog circuits and dissipative networks. We will view learning as a feedback interconnection of continuous-time (circuit) dynamics and an optimization algorithm. The key idea is to develop algorithms that minimise cost functions inspired by notions of energy, leading to highly efficient, local learning rules.
